title: Wplace (wplace.live)
genre: Browser collaborative pixel-art canvas / social sandbox (r/place-style 'paint the world' on a world map)
window_note: in window (launched July 2025, viral July–Sept 2025). Chosen over Dragonsweeper, which is OUT of window (free itch.io browser release January 2025; no Steam version found) and over Internet Roadtrip (neal.fun, May 2025, solo, but only ~1,000 concurrent players). Caveat: Wplace is a game-like collaborative canvas rather than a classic game.
developer: Murilo Matsubara (Brazilian developer) [CONFIRMED – Wikipedia; single-source attribution]
team_size: no data – press and Wikipedia name a single Brazilian developer as creator; no source gives a headcount (likely 1–3 people [ESTIMATE – based on single named creator and the developer handling community posts personally], unverified)
developer_background: no data on previous projects. Inspired by Reddit's r/place but permanent and on a real world map.
platforms_and_store_links: Web: https://wplace.live ; community browser extensions exist (e.g. Firefox add-on 'wplace-live', third-party)
business_model: Free to play in the browser. In-game currency 'droplets' (1 per pixel placed, 500 per level-up) buys more pixel capacity, faster regeneration, premium colors (32 of 63 colors cost 2,000 droplets each), profile picture and country flags [CONFIRMED – Wikipedia/Know Your Meme]. The developer addressed 'pay to win' complaints in an Aug 2025 Reddit post, implying real-money purchases exist, but no found source confirms real-money prices [no data].
units_or_downloads: 1M+ users within 4 days of launch (late July 2025) [CONFIRMED/ESTIMATE – reported by press coverage summarized on Wikipedia/ScreenHub; original source not identified]; later totals: no data. Traffic proxy: the map-tile provider OpenFreeMap recorded ~3 billion requests in 24 hours and peaks of ~100,000 requests/second from Wplace in early August 2025 [CONFIRMED – OpenFreeMap developer Zsolt Ero via Gigazine]. Strong user base in Brazil and Germany.
gross_revenue: no data (no disclosed revenue; real-money pricing not confirmed in found sources)
net_revenue: no data. If real-money droplet sales exist they would go through a web payment processor (~3% fee) with no store/portal cut.
production_cost: no disclosed figure. Build: est. 1–3 people × 1–3 months × ~$3k/month ≈ $3k–$27k opportunity cost [ESTIMATE – spec method, Brazil rate; team size unverified]. Running costs can be significant at viral scale (servers, bandwidth, moderation); map tiles came free from OpenFreeMap (donation-funded), which was overwhelmed by the traffic.
why_popular: Takes the beloved but time-limited r/place event and makes it permanent on a real world map: users paint their country, city, flags, anime/game fan art (Deltarune sprite art became a meme) and see country leaderboards. Strong identity/nationalism hook (country competition), collaborative and adversarial communities, instant browser access, and screenshot/time-lapse-friendly visuals for TikTok.
marketing_channels: Organic TikTok and short-form video, X/Twitter posts (e.g. viral Deltarune/botting threads), Reddit, Discord communities coordinating art, Know Your Meme coverage; national rivalry (Brazil, Germany) drove word of mouth. No paid marketing reported.
engine: Custom web app (browser JS) on a world map using OpenFreeMap vector tiles [CONFIRMED – OpenFreeMap traffic incident]; backend stack not disclosed (no data)
art_style: User-generated pixel art over a vector world map
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write a map-based pixel canvas (MapLibre/Leaflet + canvas tiles), auth, cooldown/currency logic, WebSocket sync and a basic moderation dashboard; generate UI art and marketing copy. | AI cannot: handle the operational side of going viral – scaling to millions of users and billions of requests (CDN, rate limiting, anti-bot), moderating offensive content and bans, community management and fair monetization (the dev faced 'pay to win', ban and downtime complaints); the novelty depends on timing and community energy. | Toolset: Claude Code + TypeScript/Next.js or SvelteKit, MapLibre GL + OpenFreeMap/Protomaps tiles, Redis/Postgres or Cloudflare Durable Objects for canvas state, WebSockets, Cloudflare CDN/Turnstile, Stripe for optional purchases.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 2–4 weeks, $100–$400 (Claude Pro/Max, domain, small VPS/Cloudflare plan; excludes living costs)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 2–4 months, $2,000–$15,000+ (mostly infrastructure/bandwidth at scale, anti-bot tooling, moderation help); costs grow with virality, so set up monetization and rate limits before launch

sources.title: Know Your Meme – What is Wplace? The viral Reddit Place copycat explained
ScreenHub – Wplace is a new online map where gamers are 'painting the world'
Click2Houston (AP) – Welcome to Wplace, a chaotic collaborative digital canvas
Gigazine – OpenFreeMap survived 100,000 requests/second from wplace.live
Know Your Meme – Deltarune Sprite Art on Wplace

data_conflicts: 1) Team size: only a single named creator found; one search summary could not confirm the creator's name, Wikipedia does – used Wikipedia. 2) Monetization: sources describe earned droplets only; the developer's 'pay to win' Reddit response (27 Aug 2025) implies paid options – real-money pricing left as no data. 3) User numbers: only the '1M users in 4 days' launch figure found; no later totals.
notes: Shows that a 'permanent, global version of a beloved limited event' can go viral with zero marketing, but also that viral web projects carry infrastructure, moderation and anti-bot costs that a solo dev must plan for (OpenFreeMap was hit with 3B requests/day). For a solo + AI creator: ship the MVP fast, but build rate limits, CDN caching and a monetization path (cosmetics, supporter perks) before launch. Other candidates checked: Dragonsweeper (Daniel Benmergui, free itch.io browser game, Jan 2025 – outside window, no Steam version found; copycats 'DungeonSweeper' appeared on Steam in 2026); Internet Roadtrip (Neal Agarwal, neal.fun, launched 2025-05-06, solo, ~1,000 simultaneous drivers).
